section_summary: This section covers U.S. State Department and diplomatic intelligence records from July 1941 to February 1944 concerning political developments and ministerial reorganizations in the Japanese government. Key subjects include the fall of the third Konoe Cabinet and the formation of the military-dominated Tojo Cabinet in October 1941, the resignation of Foreign Minister Shigenori Togo over the creation of the Ministry of Greater East Asia in late 1942, and successive wartime reallocations of economic, munitions, and foreign affairs portfolios under Hideki Tojo through early 1944. A comprehensive 21-page OSS intelligence monograph details the jurisdiction, central administration, and field organization of the Ministry of Greater East Asia across occupied territories, alongside diplomatic reporting from Tokyo, Bern, Moscow, Chungking, and London assessing Japan's continental strategy, Axis relations, and Soviet policy.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a memorandum reporting on a conversation with the Japanese Ambassador regarding the formation of a new Japanese cabinet.
subfiles.from: Sumner Welles, Under Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet notes a July 18, 1941 memorandum by Under Secretary of State Sumner Welles filed under 004.00/1094. The underlying document records a conversation with the Japanese Ambassador concerning the organization and political implications of the newly reorganized Japanese cabinet. The original record was classified under general political affairs decimal file 894.002/491.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: New Japanese Cabinet (State Department Memorandum of Conversation with Japanese Ambassador)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a confidential telegram from Tokyo reporting on an assassination attempt against Prime Minister Fumimaro Konoe.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes Telegram No. 1490 sent by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew from Tokyo on September 20, 1941, filed under 711.94/2302. The underlying communication provides confidential intelligence regarding an attempt on the life of Japanese Prime Minister Prince Fumimaro Konoe. The document was retained in the confidential bilateral relations file.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Attempt to Assassinate Prime Minister Konoe

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a telegram from China reporting rumors that the East Asia League was attempting to form a new Japanese cabinet.
subfiles.from: Richard P. Butrick, U.S. Diplomatic Officer in China
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference note records a September 19, 1941 telegram from Richard P. Butrick in China, original file number 894.00/1101. The message details intelligence and rumors concerning political maneuvers by the East Asia League to influence cabinet composition in Japan. It reflects external diplomatic monitoring of Japanese domestic political factionalism.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Rumors of New Japanese Cabinet Attempted by East Asia League

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting on the police investigation and detention of foreign journalists following the attempted assassination of Baron Kiichiro Hiranuma.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reports peculiar circumstances surrounding the assassination attempt against Minister of State Baron Kiichiro Hiranuma. Approximately ten hours before the shooting, Mr. Aloisi, the Italian Stefani News Agency representative, had telephoned the Home Ministry to verify an unconfirmed rumor that Hiranuma had been shot. Following the actual attack, Japanese police descended upon the Stefani Agency, interrogated foreign and Domei correspondents, and released Aloisi from custody only after the Italian Embassy identified two Japanese informants.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5797 from Tokyo: Attempted Assassination of Baron Hiranuma

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a telegram reporting the en masse resignation of the Konoe Cabinet and the Emperor's request that it remain temporarily in office.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: This sheet indexes Telegram No. 1643 dispatched by Ambassador Grew from Tokyo on October 16, 1941, filed under 894.00/1106. It records the official submission of the Cabinet's resignation to Emperor Hirohito at 5:00 p.m. and notes the Imperial command for ministers to remain in office until a successor government was formed.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Resignation of the Third Konoe Cabinet

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting the official announcement of the resignation of the third Konoe Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports by urgent plain wire that the Japanese government officially announced at 8:15 p.m. the resignation of the entire Cabinet, which had been tendered to the Emperor at 5:00 p.m. that afternoon. The Emperor requested that the Cabinet remain in office for the time being. This signaled the definitive collapse of the third Konoe administration amid deadlocked negotiations with the United States.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1643 from Tokyo: Announcement of Cabinet Resignation

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a telegram reporting that War Minister General Hideki Tojo had been designated to form a new cabinet.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet notes Telegram No. 1650 sent by Ambassador Grew on October 17, 1941, filed under 894.00/1107. It documents the Imperial command designating Lieutenant General Hideki Tojo, War Minister in the outgoing Konoe Cabinet, to assume the premiership and form a successor administration.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: General Tojo Designated to Form New Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a telegram listing the ministerial roster of the newly organized Tojo Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: This sheet cross-references Telegram No. 1652 from Tokyo, dated October 18, 1941, filed under 894.00/1111. It records the complete initial ministerial lineup of the Tojo administration, including Tojo holding the Premier, War, and Home portfolios concurrently, Shigenori Togo in Foreign Affairs and Overseas, Okinori Kaya in Finance, Shigetaro Shimada in Navy, and other major appointments.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Ministerial Appointments in the Tojo Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a telegram reporting Japanese public sentiment regarding the resignation of the Prime Minister and Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet notes Telegram No. 1644 sent by Ambassador Grew on October 17, 1941, filed under 894.00/1109. It reports that public opinion in Japan viewed the cabinet crisis as undesirable and urged political leaders to reaffirm their convictions in the face of national and international difficulties.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Public Reaction to Resignation of Konoe Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a telegram reporting appointments to the Planning Board, Information Board, Cabinet Secretariat, and Legislative Bureau.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: This sheet indexes Telegram No. 1655 sent by Grew on October 19, 1941, filed under 894.00/1116. It records the appointments of Teiichi Suzuki as President of the Planning Board, Masayuki Tani as President of the Information Board, Naoki Hoshino as Chief Secretary of the Cabinet, and Eiichi Moriyama as Director of the Legislative Bureau.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Supplementary Appointments to Tojo Cabinet

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting supplementary high-level appointments to executive boards and bureaus in the new Japanese Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew supplements his previous report on the new Japanese Cabinet by informing the State Department that Minister without Portfolio Teiichi Suzuki has been appointed concurrently President of the Cabinet Planning Board. Former Vice Foreign Minister Masayuki Tani was appointed President of the Information Board, Naoki Hoshino became Chief Secretary of the Cabinet, and Eiichi Moriyama was named Director of the Legislative Bureau.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1655 from Tokyo: Key Administrative Appointments in Tojo Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a telegram reporting the press announcement of Haruhiko Nishi's appointment as Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: This sheet records Telegram No. 1673 sent by Ambassador Grew on October 22, 1941, filed under 894.00/1121. It documents the Tokyo press announcement appointing Haruhiko Nishi, whose prior post was embassy counselor with the rank of minister in Moscow, as the new Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs under Shigenori Togo.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Appointment of Haruhiko Nishi as Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs

subfiles.about: Intelligence estimate analyzing the composition, aggressive continental background, and foreign policy orientation of the newly formed Tojo Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: The Division of Far Eastern Affairs presents an appraisal of the newly installed Tojo Cabinet, characterizing it as strong, predominantly military, and heavily represented by figures linked to continental expansion. The analysis identifies key challenges including settling the China conflict, overcoming ABCD economic sanctions (especially regarding oil and metals), and confronting potential US-Soviet military encirclement. While the cabinet will pursue military mobilization, the appointment of experienced diplomat Shigenori Togo suggests Japan remains open to negotiated settlements with the United States and Russia while preparing for force if talks collapse.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum: An Estimate of the Tojo Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a memorandum linking the fall of the Konoe Cabinet to the rejection by Japanese ruling factions of Konoe's negotiation terms with the U.S.
subfiles.from: F. E. Langdon, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes an October 16, 1941 memorandum by F. E. Langdon filed under 894.00/1135. It notes initial reports linking the collapse of the Konoe government to the rejection by controlling military and political factions in Japan of Prince Konoe's proposed conditions for adjusting relations with the United States.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Fall of Konoe Cabinet and Rejection of Terms for U.S.-Japan Relations

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a War Department letter transmitting intelligence on the fall of the Japanese Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Sherman Miles, Brigadier General, War Department Military Intelligence Division
subfiles.summary: This sheet records an October 16, 1941 letter from Brigadier General Sherman Miles of the War Department, filed under 894.00/1122. The communication transmits military intelligence reporting and evaluation concerning the collapse of the Konoe government in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: War Department Report on the Fall of the Japanese Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a War Department letter enclosing a United Press wire report on the resignation of the three-month-old Konoe Cabinet.
subfiles.from: War Department
subfiles.summary: This sheet indexes an October 16, 1941 War Department letter filed under 894.00/1133. The underlying item transmits a United Press news dispatch reporting the sudden resignation on October 16 of the third Konoe Cabinet after only three months in office.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: United Press Dispatch on Resignation of Konoe Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a memorandum of conversation with M. E. Denning of the British Embassy regarding the resignation of the Japanese Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet notes an October 16, 1941 memorandum by Maxwell M. Hamilton filed under 701.9411/1498. It records an inquiry from M. E. Denning of the British Embassy seeking official State Department information concerning the cabinet resignation in Tokyo, and Hamilton's reply citing Ambassador Grew's initial brief cable.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: British Embassy Inquiry Regarding Resignation of Japanese Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a confidential memorandum recording the Japanese Ambassador's statements on the Tojo Cabinet's stance toward Washington talks.
subfiles.from: Joseph W. Ballantine, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes a November 7, 1941 memorandum of conversation by Joseph W. Ballantine filed under 711.94/2540-3/35. It summarizes remarks made by Japanese Ambassador Kichisaburo Nomura regarding the attitude of the newly installed Tojo Cabinet toward ongoing diplomatic negotiations with the United States.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Japanese Ambassador's Comments on New Cabinet's Attitude Toward U.S.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a War Department communication noting press reports of General Hideki Tojo's appointment as Premier.
subfiles.from: War Department
subfiles.summary: This sheet records an October 17, 1941 communication from the War Department filed under 894.00/1134. It forwards a United Press dispatch reporting that Lieutenant General Hideki Tojo, War Minister in the late Konoe Cabinet, had been designated Premier and instructed to form a new cabinet.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: War Department Communication on General Tojo Designated Premier

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a memorandum of conversation with Ambassador Nomura and Special Envoy Kurusu regarding General Tojo's peaceful intentions.
subfiles.from: Joseph W. Ballantine, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes a November 17, 1941 memorandum by Joseph W. Ballantine filed under 711.94/2540-14/35. It records statements made during diplomatic discussions by Ambassador Kichisaburo Nomura and Special Envoy Saburo Kurusu conveying Prime Minister General Tojo's desire to reach a peaceful agreement with the United States.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Conversation with Japanese Envoys on Tojo's Desire for Peace

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a War Department report on British official opinion viewing the new Japanese cabinet as pro-Nazi and anti-Soviet.
subfiles.from: War Department
subfiles.summary: This sheet indexes an October 17, 1941 War Department report filed under 894.00/1127. It conveys official British intelligence assessments concluding that the installation of the Tojo Cabinet favored armed Japanese action against the Soviet Union and characterized the new leadership as decidedly pro-Axis and anti-Soviet.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: War Department Communication on British Views of Tojo Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a State Department memorandum detailing the roster of cabinet ministers appointed under Prime Minister Tojo.
subfiles.from: F. E. Langdon, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: This sheet records an October 20, 1941 memorandum by F. E. Langdon filed under 894.00/1136. It lists the portfolios and appointees of the new cabinet, including General Tojo as Premier, War, and Home Minister, Shigenori Togo in Foreign Affairs, Shinsuke Kishi in Communications, Okinobu Kaya in Finance, Hiroyasu Ino in Agriculture, and Kunihiko Hashida in Education.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Roster of Ministers in the New Tojo Cabinet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a telegram reporting the formal installation of former Finance Minister Seihin Ikeda as a member of the Privy Council.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, U.S. Ambassador to Japan
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet notes Telegram No. 1717 sent by Ambassador Grew on October 30, 1941, filed under 894.00/1140. It reports that Seihin Ikeda, former Finance Minister in the first Konoe Cabinet and Cabinet Advisory Councillor, was formally invested as a member of the Imperial Privy Council in an Imperial Palace ceremony.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Installation of Seihin Ikeda as Privy Councillor

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a memorandum commenting on the resignation of Taro Terasaki as Chief of the American Affairs Bureau.
subfiles.from: W. W. Smyth, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: This sheet indexes an October 29, 1941 memorandum by W. W. Smyth filed under FW894.00/1142. It refers to a report in the Washington Star stating that Taro Terasaki was relieved of his post as Chief of the Foreign Office American Affairs Bureau at his own request, analyzing the possible diplomatic significance for U.S.-Japanese relations.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Resignation of Taro Terasaki from Foreign Office American Affairs Bureau

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a biographical memorandum summarizing the military and administrative career of Lieutenant General Hideki Tojo.
subfiles.from: F. E. Langdon, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: This sheet records an October 17, 1941 memorandum by F. E. Langdon filed under 894.00/1141. It outlines the career of Premier-Designate Hideki Tojo, noting he is nearly 57 years old, served as War Minister since July 1940, spent time in Germany as a military resident officer, and previously served as Gendarmerie Commander, Chief of Staff of the Kwantung Army, and Director of Army Military Aviation.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Biographical and Career Data on Premier-Designate Hideki Tojo

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a War Department letter enclosing news reporting on the resignation of the Konoe Cabinet.
subfiles.from: War Department
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet notes an October 16, 1941 War Department letter filed under 894.00/1133. The communication transmits a United Press wire report regarding the sudden resignation of the three-month-old Konoe Cabinet on October 16.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: War Department Letter on Resignation of Konoe Cabinet

subfiles.about: Detailed analytical intelligence study outlining the ministerial roster and strategic policy orientation of the Tojo Cabinet.
subfiles.from: Far Eastern Section, Coordinator of Information
subfiles.summary: The Coordinator of Information (COI) Far Eastern Section presents a seven-point analytical appraisal of the Tojo Cabinet formed on October 18, 1941. It provides a complete ministerial lineup and argues that the cabinet concentrates power unprecedentedly under Tojo (who holds the Premiership, War, and Home Ministries), is strongly oriented toward the Axis due to ministers' German ties, and is heavily dominated by veterans of continental administration in Manchuria and China. The memorandum highlights the cabinet's design for total economic and manpower mobilization under Planning Board technocrats, points to a strategic orientation directed North toward the Soviet Union rather than South, and notes the complete absence of party politicians or business representatives.
subfiles.title: COI Far Eastern Section Memorandum No. 2: The Tojo Cabinet

subfiles.about: Memorandum analyzing the strategic implications of Shigenori Togo's resignation as Foreign Minister and Tojo's assumption of the portfolio.
subfiles.from: Max W. Bishop, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Max W. Bishop assesses radio reports from London and Berlin announcing the sudden resignation of Foreign Minister Shigenori Togo and Prime Minister Tojo's concurrent takeover of the Foreign Ministry. Bishop reviews Togo's prior diplomatic service as Ambassador to Moscow and his persistent advocacy of a negotiated settlement with the Soviet Union. The memorandum concludes that while Togo's departure does not necessarily signify an imminent outbreak of Russo-Japanese hostilities, his removal would be a logical prerequisite if Japan decided to launch an attack against Russia.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum: Resignation of Foreign Minister Togo
subfiles.to: Sumner Welles, Under Secretary of State, and Cordell Hull, Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Strictly confidential telegram reporting intelligence on the policy dispute between Togo and Tojo over the Greater East Asia Ministry.
subfiles.from: Leland Harrison, U.S. Minister to Switzerland
subfiles.summary: Minister Leland Harrison reports from Bern that the U.S. Military Attaché learned from reliable Japanese sources in Switzerland that Shigenori Togo's resignation stemmed from a direct conflict with Prime Minister Tojo. The dispute centered on the creation and jurisdiction of the proposed Ministry for Greater East Asia, which was designed to assume control over all political and administrative affairs in East Asia previously managed by the Foreign Office, drastically curtailing the diplomatic service's authority.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 4089 from Bern: Reasons for Reconstruction of Japanese Foreign Ministry

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a London telegram assessing the non-military significance of the resignations of Togo and Nishi.
subfiles.from: John G. Winant, U.S. Ambassador to Great Britain
subfiles.summary: This sheet indexes Telegram No. 6006 sent by Ambassador John G. Winant from London on September 7, 1942, filed under 740.0011 Pacific War/2793. It reports British views indicating that the resignations of Foreign Minister Shigenori Togo and Vice Foreign Minister Haruhiko Nishi represented an administrative restructuring of the Foreign Office without immediate military significance.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Resignation of Foreign Minister Togo and Vice Minister Nishi

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a telegram from Vichy conveying Tokyo information regarding Foreign Minister Togo's resignation.
subfiles.from: S. Pinkney Tuck, U.S. Chargé d'Affaires in Vichy
subfiles.summary: This sheet records Telegram No. 1303 dispatched by S. Pinkney Tuck from Vichy, France, on September 5, 1942, filed under 894.00/1162. It forwards diplomatic intelligence received from Tokyo regarding the political crisis surrounding Shigenori Togo's resignation as Japanese Foreign Minister.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Diplomatic Reporting from Vichy on Togo's Resignation

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a telegram reporting Allied views in the USSR on Togo's dismissal over jurisdictional encroachment by the Greater East Asia Ministry.
subfiles.from: U.S. Embassy in Kuibyshev (U.S.S.R.)
subfiles.summary: This sheet indexes Telegram No. 437 sent from Kuibyshev on September 2, 1942, filed under 793.94/17090. It reports that British and French diplomatic sources in the Soviet wartime capital attributed Togo's removal to his unyielding resistance against General Tojo's plan to create a Greater East Asia Ministry that would strip the Foreign Office of its core jurisdictional prerogatives.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Kuibyshev Telegram on Togo's Opposition to Greater East Asia Ministry

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a memorandum submitting radio broadcast intercepts regarding Foreign Minister Togo's resignation.
subfiles.from: Herbert S. Fales, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: This sheet indexes a September 10, 1942 memorandum by Herbert S. Fales filed under 800.76 Monitoring/382. It transmits reports compiled from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Foreign Broadcast Monitoring Service weekly review covering August 28 to September 3, 1942, concerning international broadcast coverage of Togo's departure.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: FCC Monitoring Review on Resignation of Foreign Minister Togo

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a despatch from Chungking enclosing Chinese editorial opinion on Togo's resignation and the Greater East Asia Ministry.
subfiles.from: Clarence E. Gauss, U.S. Ambassador to China
subfiles.summary: This sheet records Despatch No. 616 sent by Ambassador Clarence E. Gauss from Chungking on September 12, 1942, filed under 893.9111/43. The despatch transmits translations of Chinese press editorials analyzing the implications of the Japanese cabinet shakeup and the institutional creation of the Ministry of Greater East Asia.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Chinese Editorial Comment on Resignation of Togo and New Ministry

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a confidential telegram reporting and commenting on the designation of Kazuo Aoki to head the Ministry of Greater East Asia.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes Telegram No. 1567 of October 21, 1942, filed under 894.00/1167. It documents diplomatic reporting and analysis on the official selection of Kazuo Aoki, former Supreme Economic Adviser to the Nanking government, to head the newly established Ministry of Greater East Asia.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Appointment of Kazuo Aoki as Minister of Greater East Asia

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a Chungking despatch enclosing a Chinese newspaper article on the Greater East Asia Ministry.
subfiles.from: Clarence E. Gauss, U.S. Ambassador to China
subfiles.summary: This sheet records Despatch No. 636 sent by Ambassador Gauss from Chungking on September 21, 1942, filed under 894.00/1166. It encloses an article published in the Central Daily News (Chungking) on September 14, 1942, discussing the political friction surrounding Togo's resignation and the structural establishment of the Greater East Asia Ministry.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Central Daily News Article on Greater East Asia Ministry and Togo

subfiles.about: Intelligence report on the reorganization of Argentine army intelligence and presidential secret service under Colonel Félix María Rossi.
subfiles.from: Major Charles Hornbeck Lee and Brigadier General John W. Lang, Military Attaché, Buenos Aires
subfiles.summary: This intelligence report details the establishment of the Dirección de Vigilancia e Informaciones in Buenos Aires under Lieutenant Colonel Félix María Rossi, combining army secret service, presidential intelligence, and propaganda operations. It identifies key personnel including Lieutenant Colonel Luis Golo and Major Oscar A. Valotta, gives headquarters locations, and describes mail interception operations at the Central Post Office previously directed against Allied activities under the Castillo regime. Note: This Argentine document was filed out of place in the Japanese political affairs decimal file.
subfiles.title: Military Attaché Report No. 1552 from Buenos Aires: New Secret Service Organization

subfiles.about: Memorandum reviewing the underlying OSS study on the jurisdiction, organization, and personnel of the Japanese Greater East Asia Ministry.
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Laurence E. Salisbury submits a brief evaluation to Political Adviser Stanley K. Hornbeck regarding the attached OSS study on the Japanese Greater East Asia Ministry. Salisbury commends the memorandum as a well-constructed outline of the ministry's structure, noting that while it synthesizes available data effectively, it contains no major factual revelations beyond what Far Eastern Affairs officers had already compiled.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum: Review of OSS Report on Greater East Asia Ministry
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Adviser on Political Relations

subfiles.about: Exhaustive intelligence monograph detailing the statutory authority, central ministry bureaus, advisory councils, and overseas field structure of the Ministry of Greater East Asia.
subfiles.from: Office of Strategic Services (OSS)
subfiles.summary: This comprehensive 21-page OSS intelligence monograph provides an exhaustive organizational analysis of Japan's Ministry of Greater East Asia (Daitōashō), established in late 1942. The report defines the ministry's territorial jurisdiction encompassing all occupied and sphere areas outside Japan proper, Korea, Formosa, and Karafuto, and details its absorption of the China Affairs Board (Kōain), the Manchurian Affairs Board, the Overseas Ministry, and the Foreign Office East Asia Bureau. It profiles Minister Kazuo Aoki, Vice Minister Kumaichi Yamamoto, six specialized technical Councillors, and the four main administrative bureaus (General Affairs, Manchukuo, China, and South Seas). The study further maps the diplomatic and administrative field structure in occupied China and Inner Mongolia under Ambassador Mamoru Shigemitsu and four Ministers Plenipotentiary (at Nanking, Kalgan, Peking, and Shanghai), as well as embassy and consular representations in Manchukuo, French Indo-China, and Thailand, while noting that areas under military administration (Philippines, Malaya, Netherlands East Indies, Burma) remain outside its immediate control.
subfiles.title: OSS Research and Analysis Report: Jurisdiction, Organization and Personnel of Japanese Greater East Asia Ministry

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting diplomatic discussions with Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek concerning Japanese cabinet changes and Soviet-Polish relations.
subfiles.from: John Carter Vincent, Counselor of Embassy in Chungking
subfiles.summary: John Carter Vincent reports on an interview with Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek in Chungking. The Generalissimo stated that he preferred to withhold judgment on the recent Japanese cabinet shakeup until the new appointees had functioned for several weeks, and expressed agreement with the U.S. position regarding strained Soviet-Polish diplomatic relations. Chiang also voiced active interest in General Joseph W. Stilwell's mission and satisfaction with reports from General Thomas C. Hearn that Stilwell was optimistic. Pages 225 and 226 preserve duplicate file copies of the telegram.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 656 from Chungking: Conversation with Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek

subfiles.about: Memorandum assessing the appointment of Mamoru Shigemitsu as Foreign Minister and internal administrative consolidation in Tokyo.
subfiles.from: Max W. Bishop, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Max W. Bishop analyzes major Japanese cabinet changes in April 1943, highlighted by the appointment of career diplomat Mamoru Shigemitsu as Minister for Foreign Affairs, General Tojo's assumption of the Education portfolio, Lieutenant General Kisaburo Ando's appointment as Home Minister, and Eiji Amau's selection to head the Information Board. Bishop evaluates Shigemitsu's diplomatic qualifications—noting his experience in China, Moscow, and London—and his role in crafting Japan's 'new policy' of appeasement toward occupied China to elicit puppet cooperation. The memorandum concludes that the reorganization tightens domestic control and administrative efficiency without altering basic aggressive policies.
subfiles.title: State Department Memorandum: Changes in the Japanese Cabinet

subfiles.about: Confidential circular cable synthesizing British, Chungking, and State Department assessments of the April 1943 Japanese cabinet reorganization.
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.summary: The State Department transmits to the Embassy in Kuibyshev a synthesized intelligence assessment of Japan's April 1943 cabinet changes. The cable contrasts London reporting—which discounted journalistic speculation of peace overtures and saw Shigemitsu's appointment as consolidating gains in China—with Chungking views predicting no immediate attack on Russia or success in Chinese appeasement. Department analysts conclude that the reorganization strengthened domestic war administration, that Shigemitsu will spearhead a 'soft policy' in China to provoke civil strife, and that Japan will continue efforts to preserve Soviet neutrality and mediate a separate peace between Germany and the USSR.
subfiles.title: State Department Cable No. 221 to Kuibyshev: Analysis of Japanese Cabinet Changes

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to a Chungking despatch enclosing a memorandum of conversation on Chinese interpretations of the Japanese cabinet changes.
subfiles.from: John Carter Vincent, Counselor of Embassy in Chungking
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet notes Despatch No. 1128 sent by John Carter Vincent from Chungking on April 30, 1943, filed under 894.00/1182. It transmits a memorandum of conversation recording official and political Chinese interpretations of the significant ministerial changes announced in Tokyo earlier that month.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Chungking Despatch on Interpretations of Japanese Cabinet Changes

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting the appointment of prominent industrial leaders and planners as Cabinet Councillors to assist the Ministry of Munitions.
subfiles.from: Leland Harrison, U.S. Minister to Switzerland
subfiles.summary: Leland Harrison reports from Bern on a Tokyo DNB dispatch announcing the appointment of key Cabinet Councillors: Ginjiro Fujiwara as Minister without Portfolio, Lieutenant General Teiichi Suzuki of the Planning Board, Yoshisuke Aikawa of the Manchurian Industrial Development Company, and Keita Goto of the Tokyo Railway Company. German commentary highlighted by Harrison stresses that Fujiwara's industrial and munitions expertise is designed to make him the primary economic adviser to Premier Tojo (who had assumed the new Munitions portfolio) in structuring the state apparatus for total warfare.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 7243 from Bern: Appointment of Japanese Cabinet Councillors for Total War

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to reporting on the conduct of Japanese Foreign Office delegate Baron Yasushi Hayashi aboard the exchange ship Teia Maru.
subfiles.from: U.S. Consulate in Lourenço Marques (Preston at Mormugao)
subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes an October 27, 1943 report forwarded via Lourenço Marques from consular officer Preston at Mormugao, filed under 701.0090/3181. It comments on the attitude and activities of Consul General Baron Yasushi Hayashi, Japanese Foreign Office delegate aboard the exchange vessel Teia Maru, during the diplomatic repatriation of Japanese and American nationals in Portuguese India.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Report on Japanese Diplomatic Delegate Baron Hayashi at Mormugao Exchange

subfiles.about: Cross-reference to an official communication reporting the creation and key personnel of the Japanese Ministry of Transport and Communications.
subfiles.from: International Bureau of the Telecommunication Union
subfiles.summary: This sheet records a January 4, 1944 notification from the International Bureau of the Telecommunication Union filed under 791. It provides official notification of the establishment of the Ministry of Transport and Communications in Japan on November 1, 1943, and lists the principal administrative personnel heading the merged department.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Creation of Ministry of Transport and Communications

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting Moscow press coverage of a major Japanese cabinet reshuffle affecting Communications, Agriculture, and Finance.
subfiles.from: W. Averell Harriman, U.S. Ambassador to the U.S.S.R.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador W. Averell Harriman reports from Moscow that Soviet newspapers of February 20 published accounts of a significant Japanese cabinet reorganization. The reports stated that Minister of Communications Yoshiaki Hatta, Minister of Agriculture and Commerce Tatsunosuke Yamazaki, and Minister of Finance Okinori Kaya had been replaced respectively by Keita Goto, Nobuya Uchida, and Sotaro Ishiwata. Pages 237 through 239 preserve the received telegram, internal routing sheets, and paraphrased copies circulated within the State Department's Division of Far Eastern Affairs.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 570 from Moscow: Japanese Ministerial Replacements in Communications, Agriculture, and Finance

subfiles.about: Telegram reporting Berlin press coverage and official German assessments of the February 1944 Japanese cabinet changes.
subfiles.from: Leland Harrison, U.S. Minister to Switzerland
subfiles.summary: Minister Leland Harrison reports from Bern that German newspapers, notably the Deutsche Allgemeine Zeitung, characterize the February 1944 Tokyo cabinet changes as a technical reorganization designed to concentrate authority for total war rather than a political crisis. Citing a February 21 Tokyo dispatch, German reports affirmed that Japanese war policies were fixed for the duration, that Premier Tojo had strengthened the government's executive authority, and that incoming Finance Minister Ishiwata and Agriculture and Commerce Minister Uchida planned cautious continuations of existing economic policies.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1168 from Bern: German Press Commentary on Japanese Cabinet Reshuffle
